metadata.note: The Key System (Key Route) of the East Bay: the transbay electric trains that met the Key ferry at the Key Route Pier from 26 October 1903 and ran over the Bay Bridge to San Francisco's Transbay Terminal from 15 January 1939 until 20 April 1958, the wartime Shipyard Railway (1943-45), and the principal East Bay streetcar lines (last cars 28 November 1948). Pulled 2026-09-30 (20260930).
metadata.company_judgement: All features carry company 'Key System' and one colour, #E8751A. The transbay trains were run successively by the San Francisco, Oakland & San Jose Railway (1902), SF, Oakland & San Jose Consolidated (1908), San Francisco-Oakland Terminal Railways (1912), Key System Transit Co. (1923), Key System Ltd/Key System (1930s-1946) and Key System Transit Lines (National City Lines control from 1946); the streetcars by Oakland Transit (1898), Oakland Traction (1906), SFOTR (1912), East Bay Street Railways and East Bay Transit. These are treated as ONE company because (1) they were under common control - Borax Smith's interests (the Realty Syndicate/United Properties) owned both the train and streetcar companies until his 1913 ouster, the two were formally merged into SFOTR in 1912, and after 1923 the streetcars were a Key subsidiary/division; and (2) the public brand was continuous - the Western Railway Museum describes 'a number of commonly owned corporations' that 'East Bay residents always referred to' as the Key Route or Key System. National City Lines' 1946 stock purchase is not a split point: the operating company and its name, routes and crews continued (same treatment as Southern Pacific's control of Pacific Electric in this repo). Predecessor street railways BEFORE they entered the Smith family (Oakland Railroad Co. before 1901, OSL&H before 1901, Piedmont & Mountain View before 1898, etc.) are NOT drawn - those years belong to other companies and would need their own colours.
metadata.mode_judgement: Transbay trains are 'interurban' (Rule 7): electric multiple-unit trains linking Berkeley, Oakland, Piedmont and Emeryville with San Francisco via ferry or bridge, partly on private right of way and partly street running - an inter-community electric railway, not a city streetcar and not steam/heavy commuter rail. The Shipyard Railway (Oakland-Emeryville to Richmond) is also 'interurban'. The local car lines are 'streetcar'; the G and K shuttles that fed the trains are kept with the mode of their own lines (G was a transbay branch, K/Alcatraz a streetcar line).
metadata.geometry_quality: No Key System route relation exists in OpenStreetMap or OpenHistoricalMap (OHM has only one 'OTR/Key System A/B' disused way). Street-running sections are routed on today's OSM street centrelines by name (staged street-name Dijkstra); private rights of way that survive as paths or streets use those; the Key Route Pier, the demolished 1936 Bay Bridge East Span, the Emeryville approach, the San Francisco terminal viaduct and the Richmond end of the Shipyard Railway are hand-traced from georeferenced USGS topographic quadrangles (San Francisco 1915 1:62,500; Oakland West 1949, Oakland East 1947, Richmond 1947 and San Francisco North 1950, all 1:24,000; NAD27 converted to WGS84). Each feature's geometry_quality names its pieces and their mileage. Mileage checks: the A-line abandonment of 1950 was about 5.2 mi beyond 12th and Oak per the CPUC, traced 5.23 mi; the four last car lines (1, 2, 4, 5) totalled about 26 route miles in 1948 per the CPUC, traced about 25 mi including the shared Telegraph Ave track; the pier was 16,000-17,000 ft (3.0-3.2 mi), traced about 3.0 mi from shore to the ferry slips. All lines pass the reversal/revisit spike checks except two genuine geometries: line 11's V-shaped Oakland Ave-Linda Ave turn and the Shipyard Railway's turn from Cutting Blvd south at Canal Blvd.
metadata.shared_track_note: The Sacramento Northern (Oakland, Antioch & Eastern from September 1913) ran its own trains over Key System track from 40th St & Shafter Ave to the Key Route Pier 1913-1939 and over the bridge railway to the Transbay Terminal 1939-1941; the SN layer does not draw those legs, and the Key features here draw them only as Key System service. The Bay Bridge railway and Transbay Terminal (1939-41) were shared with the Southern Pacific Interurban Electric Railway and the Sacramento Northern, and the Key used ex-SP/IER track in Berkeley (Shattuck Ave north of Dwight Way, Henry/Sutter Sts and the Northbrae Tunnel from 1941-42; California St/Monterey Ave from 1933) and East Oakland (Bond Way to Havenscourt, 1941-50). Those layers are drawn by the SP East Bay Electric Lines and Sacramento Northern layers for their own years; the features here draw the same ground only for the years Key trains ran on it.
routes_deliberately_omitted: East Shore & Suburban Railway (Richmond, San Pablo, El Cerrito streetcars, 1904-1933): independent until the 1912 SFOTR merger and a separately branded unit after; needs its own research and possibly its own colour.

16 Leona (ex-California Railway steam line, electrified 1896, Key family from Nov 1906, ended 1 April 1936): the route from Fruitvale past Mills College to Leona Heights is only partly recoverable (Courtland Ave covers parts) and was not traced.

Shuttle and minor car lines: 22 Fruitvale Ave, 23 23rd Ave, 24 Dwight Way, 25 Park Ave, 26 90th Ave, 27 Cemetery, 32 40th St, 33 Sacramento St local, 38th Ave (15 to 1946), Euclid Ave (part of 7), Spruce St, University Ave, Hollis St, W 8th St, 8th Ave, High St loop (Alameda), Broadway Terrace, Chestnut St, and the WWII 7th St shipyard shuttle - each needs its own street list and dates.
Pre-Smith years of predecessor street railways and all horsecar years (Rule 5) - e.g. Oakland Railroad horsecars from 1869, San Pablo Ave cable 1886-99 and Piedmont cable 1890-96 under other owners.
The never-completed Key line to San Jose (built in part across Piedmont; no passenger service found) and the planned D line to Montclair.
The 1939 'X' Golden Gate International Exposition ferry trains and the two-week March 1941 A-line extension to 105th Ave (sub-year detail inside drawn features).
Key Terminal Railway / Oakland Terminal Railroad: freight only (Rule 1).

Opening date of the Westbrae branch (under construction Oct 1911); drawn from 1912.

Year the East Oakland Street Railway and Highland Park & Fruitvale lines (14, 15, 18 Park Blvd) came under Smith control; drawn from the July 1911 map as a floor.
Whether the Oakland Railroad Co. and OSL&H joined Oakland Transit in 1898 (Key System article) or 1901 (their own articles); drawn from 1901.
Downtown Oakland routings and loops of the car lines, and the exact private right of way of the B through Trestle Glen and of the 10 above Pleasant Valley Ave.
Every headway except the 1941 F/H figures (CPUC), the 1912 Piedmont Ave 10-minute figure and the Shipyard Railway's 35-40 minutes is an estimate; no Key public timetable was read.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced length 3.88 mi (no documented route mileage found for this exact piece). Built from: 2.20 mi mole: 1915 USGS 1:62,500, re-registered; 1.18 mi 1949 USGS 1:24,000 (Transit Lines); 0.50 mi Yerba Buena Ave diagonal (OSM street fragments), Tower 2 to Tower 3. THE MOLE (pier and causeway west of the Emeryville shore) is drawn from the 1915 USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 sheet, re-registered by about 240 m to match the 1949 sheet (the 1915 sheet's georeferencing is visibly offset against OSM); expect +/-100 m. The pier was rebuilt slightly to the south after the May 1933 fire; this feature draws the pre-1933 alignment for all years. East of the shore the line is hand-traced from the 1949 USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 sheet ('Transit Lines'), which shows the same approach through the Southern Pacific underpass and the Key yard. Ends at Tower 3 (Yerba Buena Ave and Adeline St), where the Berkeley lines left; A and B lines turned south at Tower 2 (Louise St), which lies on this feature.

segments.note: Transbay service began 26 October 1903 under the San Francisco, Oakland & San Jose Railway (renamed SF, Oakland & San Jose Consolidated in 1908), with the Key Route ferry from the pier end to San Francisco. Carries every Key transbay line between the pier and Emeryville. Ferry era: trains ran to the Key Route Pier (mole) for the Key ferry to San Francisco. Headway is an ESTIMATE, not from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia Key System Mole gives the 26 Oct 1903 opening and the pier history.

segments.note: Operated by the San Francisco-Oakland Terminal Railways (1912 consolidation). By 1912 Tower 3 handled up to 18 Berkeley-line trains an hour plus 6 to Piedmont (East Bay Hills Project, citing Demoro), so the combined peak service on the trunk was every few minutes. Base headway is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: EBHP Northbrae/Westbrae gallery (1912 train counts at Tower 3); Wikipedia Key System for the 1912 company.

segments.note: Key System Transit Co. after the December 1923 reorganisation. A 6 May 1933 fire destroyed the ferry terminal and the outer pier; the line was rebuilt slightly to the south. Ferry-pier service ended when trains moved to the Bay Bridge on 15 January 1939; Key cars and ferries kept running to the pier for the Golden Gate International Exposition until 29 October 1939. Headway is an ESTIMATE, not from a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia Key System Mole (1933 fire, 15 Jan 1939 transfer, Exposition service to 29 Oct 1939).
